verdict.line: You lose the exchange any time you trade autos into a Fury bar above 50, but the matchup evens out to 52% in your favor once you survive to your first item spike.

brief.thesis: Renekton's Reign of Anger passive means every auto and Q he lands builds toward a threshold that upgrades his W (Ruthless Predator) into a longer stun and boosts his Q (Cull the Meek) damage and heal, so he wants to force extended melee exchanges before you have the tools to punish that. Gwen has no ranged poke advantage in this matchup and her Hallowed Mist stays at rank 1 for most of the laning phase, so the early skirmishes are genuinely his to win. The 600-game sample still gives Gwen 52%, which means this is a lane you survive rather than dominate, and it flips once Dusk and Dawn into Shadowflame comes online.

theirWindow.what: He can land a 3-hit, 1.5s stun from W (Ruthless Predator) that also destroys any shield on you, then use E (Slice and Dice) to stick and burst with the buffed Q. Hold Hallowed Mist (W) for this moment or disengage entirely rather than trading autos.

yourWindow.what: Slice and Dice is his only gap-closer at 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s, so once it's spent he can't punish you for stepping up. Throw Snip Snip! (Q) from its 450 range and reset before Cull the Meek's self-heal comes back online at 7s.

start.why: Run this over Doran's Helm (83% pick, 51.4% WR) — you need the extra healing from the two potions to survive Renekton's early Q sustain trades, not just flat magic resist.

boots.why: 55.6% pick at 48.3% WR — the flat physical damage reduction directly softens his auto/Q/empowered-W burst combo, which matters more than the ganks you're not winning anyway.

core.why: First component of the 62.8%-winrate path — gives you the early stat block to survive to your power spike.
Second item on the highest-performing path (62.8% WR, 78 games) — this is when your Q poke starts outdamaging his sustain.
Closes out the 62.8% WR core path and is the point where he can no longer win a prolonged fight against your Q/E poke.

runes.keystoneWhy: The adaptive-force healing stacks up during the short trades you're forced into, offsetting the sustain gap created by his Q (Cull the Meek) self-heal.

summoners.why: The dominant page at 52.2% WR and 62% pick — Ignite erases the healing from his Q (Cull the Meek) when you commit to a trade, and Flash is your only answer to being caught by the empowered W stun into E combo.

playing.title: Track the Fury bar
playing.detail: Reign of Anger fills on every auto and Q hit he lands; above 50 Fury his W (Ruthless Predator) becomes a 3-hit, 1.5s stun that strips shields and his Q gets a damage and heal boost. Disengage before he crosses that line.

playing.title: Poke only when his E is down
playing.detail: Slice and Dice is his sole gap-closer at 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s cooldown. Once it's spent, step up and land Snip Snip! (Q) snips from range — he has no way to punish you back.

playing.title: Hold Hallowed Mist for real commitments
playing.detail: W stays at rank 1 (22s cooldown) until very late in your skill order per this build's path, so don't burn it on chip damage — save it for when he actually dashes in to stun you.

playing.title: Reset off Skip 'n Slash hits
playing.detail: E (Skip 'n Slash) refunds cooldown when it connects, so dash in, land the hit during your attack-speed window, and leave — don't stand in his stun range to auto-trade.

playing.title: Ignite his all-ins
playing.detail: Any all-in he makes above 50 Fury is backed by a bigger Q heal; burning Ignite the moment he commits removes that sustain and turns the fight back in your favor.

playing.title: Play for CS, not kills, before level 6
playing.detail: This lane is measured with a solo-kill and lane advantage for him — don't force trades looking for an early kill. Farm through Q pokes and wait for Dusk and Dawn into Shadowflame.

playing.title: Respect Dominus commitments
playing.detail: R (Dominus) grants him bonus health and periodic Fury regeneration while active. If he transforms, disengage from prolonged fights rather than trading damage — he wins the extended exchange during that window.

brief.patchCaveat: Build order, boots, runes, and summoner spells above are pulled from measured OP.GG games on the current patch (16.18.1); the tactical reasoning — Fury thresholds, cooldown windows, and when to trade or disengage — is my own read, not part of the measured data.
